transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, nice to meet you, Doc. I guess I'm here because things have just been really tense lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve just been... well, snapping at my wife over little house things. And I'm putting off jobs and paperwork that I usually stay right on top of. 

It's frustrating because I just can’t seem to get my head quiet. Even when I go out to the workshop to get away for a bit, or when I try to go fishing, I just can't shut my brain off. I figured I needed to come talk to somebody about it.
When exactly did you first notice these feelings of tension and not being able to quiet your mind—was it right around the time your father-in-law moved in, or were you experiencing this before that?

No, it wasn't before that. He moved in with us after he had a fall, and... well, I'd say it was within the first couple of months of him being there that I noticed it all starting. That's when I realized I was already falling behind on my paperwork, and my wife and I were arguing over little household changes. So yeah, it definitely started right after he got there, not before.
Besides the tension and racing thoughts, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless about things in general?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I don't feel... sad, or hopeless, no. It's more just this constant frustration. I mean, I get annoyed easily right now, but I'm not sitting around feeling down in the dumps. It's really just the tension and not being able to focus that's getting to me.
How long have these feelings of tension and racing thoughts been going on now? Are we talking weeks, a couple of months, or longer?
It's been going on for about five months now. Like I said, it started up shortly after he moved into the house, and it's just been a constant thing since then.
If your father-in-law were to move out tomorrow, do you think these feelings of tension and racing thoughts would go away, or do you think they would continue?

I think... well, I'd like to think they would go away. But honestly, the situation hasn't really ended. He's still living with us, and all the extra work and changes around the house are still just part of our daily life now. So I haven't really had a chance to see what would happen, you know? I haven't had a stretch where things went back to normal to even know if the tension would stop.

When you're away from the house—say, at work or out fishing—do you find yourself worrying about things other than the situation with your father-in-law, or is the tension and racing thoughts mainly connected to thinking about what's happening at home?

Well, I'm actually not working right now, so I don't have a job to go to. But when I do get out of the house... like if I go fishing or just run to the store... no, I don't really find myself worrying about other things. 

It's pretty much all tied to the house. Even when I'm away, my mind just kind of loops back to my father-in-law and the whole situation there. I'm not sitting there stressing about anything else, really... it's just that one main thing.

When you're lying in bed at night trying to sleep, or in those quiet moments when you're not actively thinking about your father-in-law or the situation at home, do you still feel that tension and racing thoughts, or does it mainly come up when you're thinking about what's going on at the house?

Well... if I actually manage to get my mind off it, then no, I don't really feel all wound up. Like, if I'm lying in bed and somehow get distracted by a book or I'm just thinking about fishing, my body relaxes. I don't just feel tense out of nowhere. 

The problem is just that... well, it's really hard to keep my mind off the house. So it feels like it's always there, but yeah, the racing thoughts and the tension, they really only happen when I'm actively thinking about him and everything going on.
Before your father-in-law moved in, would you say you were generally a worrier? Did you tend to feel anxious or tense about things in your life even when there wasn't a specific problem going on?

No, not really. I mean... before he moved in, I was pretty easygoing, I think. I didn't just sit around worrying about things out of the blue. 

If a specific problem came up, sure, I'd deal with it and maybe stress a little, but I never really felt tense or anxious like this when things were just going along normally. It's really just been since all this extra pressure started at the house. Before that, I was fine.
